author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of self-denial and the casting away all selfishness

verses.text: “My Son, thou canst not possess perfect liberty unless thou altogether deny thyself.
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, you cannot possess perfect liberty unless you altogether deny yourself.

verses.text: All they are enslaved who are possessors of riches, they who love themselves, the selfish, the curious, the restless; those who ever seek after soft things, and not after the things of Jesus Christ; those who continually plan and devise that which will not stand.
verses.modernizedText: All are enslaved who are possessors of riches, who love themselves, the selfish, the curious, the restless; those who ever seek after soft things, and not after the things of Jesus Christ; those who continually plan and devise that which will not stand.

verses.text: For whatsoever cometh not of God shall perish.
verses.modernizedText: For whatever does not come from God will perish.

verses.text: Hold fast the short and complete saying, ‘Renounce all things, and thou shalt find all things; give up thy lust, and thou shalt find rest.’
verses.modernizedText: Hold fast the short and complete saying, ‘Renounce all things, and you will find all things; give up your lust, and you will find rest.’

verses.text: Dwell upon this in thy mind, and when thou art full of it, thou shalt understand all things.”
verses.modernizedText: Dwell upon this in your mind, and when you are full of it, you will understand all things.”

verses.text: O Lord, this is not the work of a day, nor children’s play; verily in this short saying is enclosed all the perfection of the religious.
verses.modernizedText: O Lord, this is not the work of a day, nor children’s play; truly in this short saying is enclosed all the perfection of the religious.

verses.text: “My son, thou oughtest not to be turned aside, nor immediately cast down, because thou hast heard the way of the perfect.
verses.modernizedText: “My son, you ought not to be turned aside, or immediately cast down, because you have heard the way of the perfect.

verses.text: Rather oughtest thou to be provoked to higher aims, and at the least to long after the desire thereof.
verses.modernizedText: Rather you ought to be stirred to higher aims, and at least to long for the desire of it.

verses.text: Oh that it were so with thee, and that thou hadst come to this, that thou wert not a lover of thine own self, but wert ready always to My nod, and to his whom I have placed over thee as thy father.
verses.modernizedText: Oh that it were so with you, and that you had come to this, that you were not a lover of yourself, but were always ready at My nod, and at that of him whom I have placed over you as your father.

verses.text: Then shouldest thou please Me exceedingly, and all thy life should go on in joy and peace.
verses.modernizedText: Then you would please Me exceedingly, and all your life would go on in joy and peace.

verses.text: Thou hast still many things to renounce, which if thou resign not utterly to Me, thou shalt not gain what thou seekest.
verses.modernizedText: You still have many things to renounce, which if you do not resign utterly to Me, you will not gain what you seek.

verses.text: I counsel thee to buy of Me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich,(1) that is heavenly wisdom, which despiseth all base things.
verses.modernizedText: I counsel you to buy from Me gold tried in the fire, that you may be rich,(1) that is heavenly wisdom, which despises all base things.

verses.text: Put away from thee earthly wisdom, and all pleasure, whether common to men, or thine own.
verses.modernizedText: Put away from yourself earthly wisdom, and all pleasure, whether common to men, or your own.

verses.text: “I tell thee that thou must buy vile things with those which are costly and great in the esteem of men.
verses.modernizedText: “I tell you that you must buy vile things with those which are costly and great in the esteem of men.

verses.text: For wonderfully vile and small, and almost given up to forgetfulness, doth true heavenly wisdom appear, which thinketh not high things of itself, nor seeketh to be magnified upon the earth; many honour it with their lips, but in heart are far from it; it is indeed the precious pearl, which is hidden from many.”
verses.modernizedText: For true heavenly wisdom appears wonderfully vile and small, and almost given up to forgetfulness; it does not think high things of itself, or seek to be magnified upon the earth; many honor it with their lips, but in heart are far from it; it is indeed the precious pearl, which is hidden from many.”
